title: Styling & Client State in Next.js: Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on styling a Next.js App Router app (CSS Modules, global CSS, Tailwind, CSS-in-JS limits) and managing client state (useState, context, Zustand, URL search params, flash-free theming).

chapters.title: Styling Mental Model: CSS Modules and Global CSS
points: CSS Modules: file named *.module.css; import styles from './x.module.css' and use className={styles.card}; class names are hashed per file so they never collide
Module selectors must contain at least one local class; bare element selectors (h1 {}) are not allowed in a module unless paired with a class, or wrapped in :global(...)
Global CSS: import './globals.css' only in the root app/layout.tsx; it applies to every route and holds resets, CSS variables and base typography
Compose multiple classes with template strings or clsx: className={`${styles.btn} ${styles.primary}`}; the styles object keys are the class names (camelCase is easiest to access)
CSS Modules vs global CSS: Modules = scoped per component and work in Server and Client Components; global = site-wide and order-dependent, so keep it minimal

chapters.title: Tailwind Setup and Daily Usage
points: Install: npm i tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss; add the plugin to postcss.config.mjs as plugins: { '@tailwindcss/postcss': {} }
Tailwind v4 loads via a single line in globals.css: @import "tailwindcss"; the old tailwind.config.js and three @tailwind directives are not needed by default
Customise with @theme in CSS: @theme { --color-brand: #0a7; } generates utilities like bg-brand and text-brand
Utilities are static class strings found by scanning source; build classes dynamically like `bg-${color}-500` and they are never generated, so map to full literal class names instead
Variants stack: hover:, focus:, md:, dark: (e.g. md:flex dark:bg-zinc-900); Tailwind works in Server Components because it is plain CSS with no runtime

chapters.title: CSS-in-JS and Server Components
points: Runtime CSS-in-JS (styled-components, Emotion) relies on React context and hooks to inject styles, so it works only in Client Components and needs 'use client'
Server Components cannot use hooks, context or browser APIs; a runtime CSS-in-JS library imported there fails at build or render
SSR with runtime CSS-in-JS needs a style registry (collect styles during render and flush them with useServerInsertedHTML) in a client provider wrapping children, or styles flash unstyled
Runtime styling also adds JS bundle weight and re-serialises styles on each render; zero-runtime options (CSS Modules, Tailwind, Panda CSS, vanilla-extract) extract CSS at build time
Rule of thumb for new App Router projects: use CSS Modules or Tailwind for server-rendered UI and keep runtime CSS-in-JS only inside isolated client islands

chapters.title: Client State: useState, Context and Zustand
points: useState holds local state, so the component must be a Client Component ('use client'); lift state up to the nearest common parent when siblings share it
Context shares state without prop drilling: create a Provider as a Client Component and render it in layout.tsx wrapping {children}; Server Components can still be passed as children through it
Context caveat: every consumer re-renders whenever the provider value changes, so split contexts by concern and memoise the value object

Zustand: const useStore = create((set) => ({ count: 0, inc: () => set(s => ({ count: s.count + 1 })) })); read with a selector, useStore(s => s.count), so a component re-renders only when that slice changes

Zustand on the server: a module-level store is shared across all requests and leaks data between users; create the store per request inside a provider (createStore with useRef) and never read it in Server Components

chapters.title: URL Search Params and Theming Without Flash
points: URL state is shareable, bookmarkable and survives refresh and back/forward; use it for filters, sort, page and tabs, and keep ephemeral UI state (modals, input drafts) in useState
Read on the server with the page prop: searchParams is a Promise in recent Next.js, so write const { q } = await searchParams; using it makes the route dynamically rendered

Read on the client with useSearchParams() (read-only URLSearchParams) and write with router.push(`?${params}`) or router.replace after building new URLSearchParams(searchParams); useSearchParams without a Suspense boundary can bail out static rendering of the whole page

Flash of wrong theme happens because the server cannot know the saved theme; fix with a tiny blocking inline script in <head> that sets the class or data-theme on <html> before first paint, plus suppressHydrationWarning on <html>

Prefer cookie-based theme so the server can render the right class directly, or use next-themes (attribute='class', defaultTheme='system'); define colours as CSS variables per theme and toggle only the attribute; also set color-scheme

chapters.title: Styling and State Cheat Sheet
points: Styling picker: CSS Modules = scoped component CSS, Tailwind = utility classes with no runtime, global CSS = resets and variables in the root layout only, runtime CSS-in-JS = Client Components only

State picker: useState = local; context = shared subtree, rerenders all consumers; Zustand = global store with selectors; URL params = shareable and bookmarkable state; cookie = server-readable preference

Top gotchas: dynamic Tailwind class names are never generated; module-level Zustand store leaks between requests; useSearchParams needs Suspense; searchParams must be awaited and makes the route dynamic
Theme flash fix checklist: blocking inline script or cookie, suppressHydrationWarning on <html>, CSS variables per theme, color-scheme set
Interview Point: why runtime CSS-in-JS breaks in Server Components, how to share state across Server and Client trees, why filters belong in the URL, how to stop theme flash
